items.title: Benjamin Franklin's London Printing 1725–26
items.venue: Papers of the Bibliographical Society of America
items.note: Assigns most items in a list of Palmer and Watts printing-house output to those shops for the first time, with the method set out.

items.title: Who was "A. Moore"? The Attribution of Eighteenth-Century Publications with False and Misleading Imprints
items.venue: Papers of the Bibliographical Society of America
items.note: Shows from ornaments that the fictitious "A. Moore" covered several printing houses, attributing some imprints and leaving several ornament groups unassigned.

items.title: An Introduction to Compositor (first posted for Fleuron, the project's original name)
items.note: Introduces a database of printers' ornaments extracted by computer vision from ECCO page images, the first searchable cross-printer ornament corpus.

items.title: Damaged Type and Areopagitica's Clandestine Printers
items.who: C. N. Warren, P. Williams, S. Rijhwani and M. G'Sell
items.note: Attributes Areopagitica to Matthew Simmons and Thomas Paine from damaged type across 100 pamphlets, the methodological model for type-based attribution.

items.title: Fleuron is now Compositor
items.note: Database relaunched at Birmingham as Compositor with keyword tagging and an image search that returns matching or similar ornaments across the corpus.

items.title: John Darby and the Whig Canon
items.note: Uses bibliographical methods to establish the output of the printer John Darby, linking his presswork to a coordinated programme of opposition whig publishing.

items.title: Canst Thou Draw Out Leviathan with Computational Bibliography? New Angles on Printing Thomas Hobbes' "Ornaments" Edition
items.who: C. N. Warren, A. Wiscomb, P. Williams, S. V. Lemley and M. G'Sell
items.note: Attributes the falsely dated "Ornaments" Leviathan to John Richardson from damaged type and proposes a new date, revising Noel Malcolm's attribution.

items.title: The Poet and the Publisher: The Case of Alexander Pope, Esq., of Twickenham versus Edmund Curll, Bookseller in Grub Street
items.note: Study of the Pope–Curll feud, covering Curll's prosecutions and the publishing practices behind them.

items.title: Computer Vision and the Creation of a Database of Printers' Ornaments
items.who: H. Wilkinson, J. Briggs and D. Gorissen
items.note: Describes extracting over a million ornament images from 33 million ECCO pages and refining them by machine learning, with the method's limits.

items.title: Libel and Lampoon: Satire in the Courts, 1670–1792
items.note: History of satire and libel prosecution after licensing, explaining the legal risks that drove concealment by authors and the trade.

items.title: Freedom and the Press before Freedom of the Press: Tools, Data and Methods for Researching Secret Printing
items.who: C. Warren, M. G'Sell, S. Lemley and M. Lincoln (Carnegie Mellon)
items.note: US$324,931 grant to build tools for analysing type and paper in late seventeenth- and eighteenth-century English printing.

items.title: Contrastive Attention Networks for Attribution of Early Modern Print
items.who: N. Vogler, K. Goyal et al.
items.venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
items.note: Metric-learning model that matches uniquely damaged type impressions across digitized books while tolerating inking and imaging noise.

items.title: Who was "A. Moore"? Waste Paper as a Means of Identification
items.venue: Papers of the Bibliographical Society of America
items.note: Uses waste sheets in booksellers' trade sale catalogues to argue that Thomas Warner published as "A. Moore", a documentary route alongside ornaments.

items.title: Relaunch of the English Short-Title Catalogue (beta) on the CERL platform
items.who: ESTC (British Library and ESTC North America) with CERL
items.note: Restores free access to ESTC, unavailable since the October 2023 British Library cyber-attack, which the corpus of unsigned imprints depends on.

items.title: Image Reuse in Eighteenth-Century Book History: Large-Scale Data-Driven Study of Headpiece Ornament Variants
items.who: R. Wang, L. Pivovarova, Y. Ryan, E. Yılandiloğlu and M. Tolonen
items.note: Computational study of headpiece variants that finds networks of printers and publishers sharing images, complicating one-block-one-owner attribution.

items.title: Catalog of Distinctive Type (CDT), Restoration England (1660–1700)
items.who: Print and Probability project and CMU Libraries
items.note: Public catalogue of about 20,000 damaged type impressions linked to over 240 London printers, described as publicly available in May 2026.
